about: The panel run: live sites to look at BY EYE on a 3D panel before a browser / SDK release, with the decision each one should get. It complements sites.json (the headless no-harm corpus): that one measures cost and outcome, this one is what a person judges. `expect` is the automatic decision (object = display rig for the whole page; world = camera rig for the whole page; object-like = camera rig with the focus from the core glass; none = not converted; standdown = the page uses the SDK). Run tools: none here; open each URL in the DisplayXR Browser. Last full pass: 2026-11-27 (v0.8.1 dev bundle), decisions below as observed.
check: the rig named in the log line `style: ...` matches `expect`, and never changes afterwards
orbit, zoom (wheel) and any fly / walk mode: no difference from the 2D page other than depth; nothing leaves and comes back
the canvas is never shown as a raw side-by-side pair, on a fresh browser launch too
object pages: the subject straddles the glass, about a third of it in front, at every angle
world pages: the focus does not hunt
the pointer over a subject that comes out of the glass is drawn in front of it (3D cursor)

sites.note: landing-page sample; the camera starts inside the splat volume
landing-page sample; decided about 3 s after load
orbit AND fly mode on one page: the display rig through both; compressed splat, glass from the bounding box
fly-native; heavy (about 15 fps in 3D on the reference box)
declared hotspots: camera rig from the start, hotspots stay on their points
slow to load (40 s); legacy post effects per eye
Babylon.js gives no surface to read: always the camera rig, focus on the camera's target
WebGPU PostProcessing chains are not split per eye yet: stays 2D by design until they are
orthographic camera at the start screen: stays 2D
its own engine, no adapter: staying 2D cleanly is the pass
